name: API Error Recovery
description: Makes TPM resilient to transient server-side API errors when delegating to subagents: on a qualifying infra failure (529 Overloaded, 5xx, 429, model temporarily unavailable) it checks Claude status, backs off, and redeploys a fresh subagent with the same task, up to a hard retry cap. Never auto-retries a genuine task failure.

posture.label: Posture
posture.description: How TPM handles a transient API failure. autonomous (default): checks Claude status and retries automatically, posting one line per attempt. ask: reports the failure and waits for approval before retrying.

maxRetries.label: Max Retries
maxRetries.description: Hard cap on retry attempts for a single failed delegation before TPM stops and escalates to the user. Non-relaxable. Attempt 1 is the first redeploy after the original failure.

backoffSeconds.label: Backoff Seconds
backoffSeconds.description: Comma-separated wait times in seconds before each retry attempt, in order. The last value repeats if there are more attempts than values. Empty means no wait.

checkStatusPage.label: Check Status Page
checkStatusPage.description: When on (default), TPM checks the Claude status page and reports the incident before retrying. When off, it skips straight to backoff and redeploy. A failed fetch never blocks recovery.

statusUrl.label: Status URL
statusUrl.description: Read-only URL TPM GETs for Claude service health. Fetched only when Check Status Page is on.

retriableErrors.label: Retriable Error Signatures
retriableErrors.default: 529, 500, 502, 503, 504, 429, Overloaded, API Error, terminated early due to an API error, overloaded_error, temporarily unavailable
retriableErrors.description: Comma-separated status codes and text markers that mark a subagent failure as a retriable infra error. Anything not matching here is a genuine task failure and is never auto-retried.

reduceConcurrencyOnOverload.label: Reduce Concurrency On Overload
reduceConcurrencyOnOverload.description: When on (default), an overload/429 failure makes TPM reduce parallelism and stagger dispatch on redeploy. When off, TPM redeploys at the same concurrency. Applies only to overload/rate-limit failures.
